original_title: Ubisoft Gives Free PC Copies to Xbox Owners of Select Games
summary_en: Ubisoft is expanding its partnership with Xbox, offering PC versions of several popular titles to Xbox owners. This move significantly benefits players who have transitioned to PC gaming.
ai_analysis: This cross-platform promotion highlights Ubisoft's strategy to maximize player engagement and leverage its existing player base across different ecosystems.

en.title: Ubisoft Gives Xbox Owners Free PC Copies of Select Games
en.summary: Ubisoft is expanding its partnership with Xbox, offering PC versions of several popular titles to Xbox owners. This move significantly benefits players who have transitioned to PC gaming.
en.body:
Ubisoft has announced a significant expansion of its partnership with Xbox, a move that directly benefits players who own select titles on Xbox consoles. Starting immediately, anyone who owns certain Ubisoft games on Xbox will receive a free PC copy through Ubisoft Connect. This generous offer applies to a robust list of popular franchises, aiming to reward existing players and encourage cross-platform play.

The titles included in this promotion are: **Assassin’s Creed Mirage**, **Assassin’s Creed Valhalla**, **Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora**, **Far Cry 6**, **Immortals Fenyx Rising**, **Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown**, **Riders Republic**, **Skull and Bones**, **The Crew 2**, **The Crew Motorfest**, **Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Extraction**, and **Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Siege**. For those who have already purchased or will purchase these games on Xbox, the corresponding PC version should automatically appear in their Ubisoft Connect library by August 4th, provided their Xbox and Ubisoft accounts are linked. Furthermore, if you buy any of these games on Xbox in the future, you will automatically receive the PC version. It's important to note that this offer is a one-way street; purchasing these games on PC will not grant you a free Xbox copy.

## A Win for PC Transitioners

This initiative is a fantastic boon for players who have made the switch from console to PC gaming. Many gamers maintain libraries across multiple platforms, and Ubisoft’s decision to bridge this gap for select titles removes a significant barrier. It acknowledges the evolving landscape of player habits, where individuals might start on one platform and later migrate to another for performance, preference, or access to a wider ecosystem. The inclusion of major titles like **Assassin's Creed Mirage** and **Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora** makes this a particularly compelling offer. Beyond this direct giveaway, Ubisoft has also bolstered its presence on Xbox's PC app, adding premium editions of games like the upcoming **Assassin's Creed Shadows**, further integrating its offerings across platforms.

## Community Reaction and Xbox's PC Push

The gaming community has largely reacted positively to this news, viewing it as a player-friendly move that increases accessibility. This promotion aligns with a broader trend observed in Xbox's recent strategic decisions, which have increasingly leaned towards PC integration. While the exact nature of this strategy remains speculative, it follows recent moves like making select original Xbox backward-compatible titles available on PC. Rumors also suggest Microsoft is exploring ways to digitize physical game libraries, potentially preparing for a more PC-centric next-generation Xbox console. This Ubisoft partnership could be a calculated step in that direction, making their ecosystem more appealing and unified for players who engage with games across different hardware.

## What's Next

Players should ensure their Xbox and Ubisoft Connect accounts are linked to receive their free PC copies. The games are expected to appear in Ubisoft Connect libraries by next week, with ongoing purchases on Xbox automatically granting PC access. It remains to be seen if this partnership will expand to include more titles or if future promotions will offer a two-way benefit for cross-platform purchases.

If you happen to purchase these games on Xbox later, you will get them on PC automatically. Unfortunately, this doesn't go both ways. If you buy one of these games on PC first, you will not get it on Xbox. If you're someone who previously played on console, but made the jump to PC, this is a great benefit. Additionally, Ubisoft has also added a bunch of premium editions for Ubisoft games like Assassin's Creed Shadows to Xbox's PC app. Recently, Xbox has been making a lot of moves toward PC. It's unclear if this is all part of one big deliberate plan or if it's coincidental, but last week, Xbox made select backward-compatible titles for the OG Xbox available on PC . More titles are expected to be added in the future. There are also rumors that Microsoft is planning a feature that will let players digitize their physical games library , possibly ahead of the next Xbox console. However, with this ongoing shift toward PC, it could make them accessible on PC.
